<pasted_content id="5d06">
[megabrain dispatch: conversation view] —  — Run megabrain received before work. Ask coordinator with megabrain ask "question"; wait with megabrain check and confirm using megabrain ack <delivery-id>. Finish with megabrain done "short outcome summary". Do not print protocol markers or continue past unanswered question. For megabrain done and ask, start with one plain-language sentence a non-technical person understands: what changed, or what you need. Use no file names, commands, or test counts in that sentence; put technical detail after it. —  — Dispatch identity: dispatch-20261015053353886-12514-d0644a5b —  — LANE C: the conversation view of a chat (issue 114). Branch feat/desktop-conversation in the megabrain repo. Work only in apps/desktop/src/chat/ (Conversation.tsx, ChatView.tsx, and new files you add there). —  — GOAL — A chat in the desktop app should read like an agent IDE such as Orca or Cursor: the person's messages, the agent's replies, its thinking, its tool calls and their results, updating live. Today apps/desktop/src/chat/Conversation.tsx is a placeholder that lists events as plain text; replace it. —  — DATA (already defined, do not change apps/desktop/src/api/) — api.transcript(target, since?) returns a Transcript (apps/desktop/src/api/schema.ts: transcriptSchema). Events have kind user, assistant, thinking, tool-call, tool-result or system, a stable id, a text, and for tools a tool object with name, input and status. The mock in apps/desktop/src/api/fixtures/mock.ts (mockTranscript) has every kind. The real CLI command is being built in parallel; build against the contract and the mock. —  — DESIGN (the app's theme is in apps/desktop/src/styles.css and src/components/ui.tsx: AMOLED black, glass, large type, very rounded; follow it) — - User messages: right-aligned rounded bubbles, subtle accent tint. — - Assistant messages: left, plain text, paragraphs kept, code fences shown as monospace blocks and inline code as monospace (write a small formatter; do not add a markdown dependency). — - Thinking: collapsed by default into one dim row (for example a small orb and the first line), expandable to the full text in dim italic. — - Tool calls: one compact row each with the tool name and a one-line input, paired with the tool-result that follows it; a status mark (ok, error, or running when no result yet); expandable to show the full input and result in a monospace block with a max height. — - System events: small centered dim text. — - Live: when live is true, poll every 2 seconds passing the last cursor as since, append new events without duplicates (by id), keep the view pinned to the bottom when the person is at the bottom, and show a Jump to latest button when they scrolled up. — - Loading, empty and error states. — - Keep the Conversation component's props as they are: { target, live }. Another lane uses it inside columns. —  — TESTS — Put the pure logic in apps/desktop/src/chat/conversation-model.ts with tests in conversation-model.test.ts: pairing tool calls with their results, merging appended events without duplicates and in order, grouping consecutive events if you do that, the code-fence formatter. —  — COMMITS (in this order) — 1. test(desktop): render a chat as a conversation  (model tests only; must fail) — 2. feat(desktop): render a chat as a conversation  (model, Conversation.tsx, any ChatView.tsx touch-ups) —  — GATES (yours), in apps/desktop: bun run typecheck && bun test src — You have no browser and should not try one; the visual check is mine. Describe what you built. —  — RULES FOR EVERY LANE — - Work only in the worktree this dispatch opened for you. Run git rev-parse --show-toplevel before your first edit and confirm it ends in the branch folder named above. — - Commits: English, conventional (type(scope): subject under 60 chars), atomic, exactly the list given above. A mixed commit is a failed task. No Co-Authored-By or any other trailer. No amend, reset or rebase. — - Tests first: the test commit comes before the implementation commit and must fail when run alone. Never weaken a test to make it pass; if a test looks wrong, ask. — - Safety: never write to ~/.megabrain, ~/.claude, ~/.codex, ~/.grok or ~/.gemini (reading them is allowed). Any test or manual run of megabrain must export MEGABRAIN_STATE_DIR to a mktemp -d directory and unset MEGABRAIN_DISPATCH_ID. Never run megabrain ask, done, hook or received as a test. Never use the default tmux server in tests. Never open a visible window or browser. Never run orb stop or orb start. — - Repo style: TypeScript strict, no any, no non-null assertion, no ==, use ?? where it fits. Match the surrounding code. — - If a decision is ambiguous, ask instead of guessing: run megabrain ask "your question", then poll with megabrain check --timeout 600 until the reply arrives. Do not proceed on a default. — - Report completion is non-negotiable: the work is not finished until you run megabrain done "summary" with what you changed, the git log --oneline of your commits, and the gate commands you ran with their pass and fail counts. Plain text, no backticks. —  — SETUP — The worktree is fresh: run bun install at the repository root, and bun install in apps/desktop if you touch the app, before anything else.
</pasted_content id="5d06">
